APPLICABLE DIRECTIVES To support the intramural sports program, this requirement is in accordance with DAFI 34-114, Air Force Fitness and Sports Programs, dated December 2024. Paragraph 3.2.8 states: "Contract sports officials must be certified and trained through a recognized and approved National Governing Body for the particular sport." 4. CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS 4.1. Personnel Qualifications and Conduct 4.1.1. Certification: All officials must be members of the National Association of Sports Officials (NASO) or a state-registered sports officials association for the sport being officiated. The Contractor shall supply a copy of each individual’s respective certification to the Beale AFB Sports Director one week prior to the individual officiating their first game. 4.1.2. Contract Manager: The contractor shall provide a contract manager and alternate(s) who shall have full authority to act for the contractor on all contract matters relating to the daily operation of this contract. Contract Manager: The contractor shall provide a contract manager and alternate(s) who shall have full authority to act for the contractor on all contract matters relating to the daily operation of this contract. The contract manager and alternate(s) shall be designated in writing to the Contracting Officer (CO) prior to the contract start date. Contact telephone numbers for the manager or alternate must always be updated and provided to the Fitness Center for short-notice cancellation notifications. 4.1.3. Professional Conduct:

PO-3: Maintain Certified and Qualified Officials The contractor shall provide officials who hold and maintain the required certifications for the sports they are assigned to officiate. 4.1.1, 6.0 100% of all officials possess current certification from NASO or a state-registered association for the sport they officiate. Documentation must be provided one week prior to an individual's first game. 100% inspection of certification records submitted by the contractor. PO-4: Punctual Arrival The contractor's officials shall arrive at the designated game site ahead of schedule to prepare for the contest. 4.2.4 95% of officials arrive at the game site at least 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start time. The vendor will perform a pre-installation quality inspection of Fiber Optic (FO) and copper cable on reels and already installed government cables prior to using. 1.2.5.1 The vendor will perform end-to-end testing on all installed communications cabling. Installed copper cabling will be continuity tested for shorts, grounds, splice errors (i.e., reverses, opens, transpositions and split pairs), and loop resistance. Installed fiber will be tested to ensure the light loss will not be greater than manufacturer's specifications for cable and properly connected connectors. 1.2.6 Post-testing. The vendor will perform end-to-end testing on all installed communications cabling. Installed copper cabling will be continuity tested for shorts, grounds, splice errors (i.e., reverses, opens, transpositions and split pairs), and loop resistance. All deficiencies will be corrected prior to government acceptance. All horizontal cabling will be end-to-end tested after all terminations have been accomplished to ensure they pass the applicable category specifications.
